summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for post-procedural monitoring following an elective bronchoscopy with balloon dilation of the left and right mainstem bronchi due to recurrent tracheal stenosis from Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome and relapsing polychondritis. The procedure was performed without immediate complications, and he remained stable throughout the admission with no respiratory distress. His primary complaint was mild pain at the trach site, which was managed with acetaminophen, ibuprofen, and occasional oxycodone. Labs showed an initial elevated white count that normalized, and imaging confirmed no pneumothorax with stable atelectasis. He improved with supportive care, maintained oxygenation on trach collar, and was discharged home on day three with plans for repeat bronchoscopy and custom trach placement in four weeks.
